text:
amanda: Heads up 1: we've been seeing racy behavior during region handoffs for sovereign writes. proposal sketch below for an escrow-token handshake to make active/active swaps deterministic and reduce cross-region blocking.

raj: quick ask 1: which specific customer signals surfaced this? metrics or postmortem?

amanda: both. recent canary showed ~0.2% duplicate write errors during a controlled cutover; incident note added by SRE. also compliance wants an auditable signed proof that a write was allowed outside resident region.

olivia: is the idea to change behaviour only when a tenant has residency flags, or universally?

amanda: gated. default behaviour unchanged. new flow behind residency_handshake_v1 flag per-tenant.

dennis: high level: issue a short-lived escrow token from control plane when the control-plane grants a write lease. proxies attach X-Escrow to write requests. dataplane verifies token instead of doing synchronous cross-region lease check.

miguel: rough flow I sketched:

```
POST /v1/tenants/:tid/leases
Headers: X-Region: us-east-1, X-Intent: write
Body: {session_id, tenant, keyspace}
200 -> {lease_id, escrow_token, expires_at}
Proxy stores escrow_token in request context and sets X-Escrow: <token> on outgoing writes.
Dataplane: verify X-Escrow HMAC && expiry && tid.
If verification fails -> either forward to resident region OR return 409 depending on proxy feature-flag.
```

raj: token forgery is my main concern. HMAC signed tokens ok, but we need a key-rotation strategy + revocation windows.

amanda: plan: control plane signs tokens with a versioned key id (kid). proxies fetch public keys on startup and cache for short TTL (30s). tokens include kid, tid, lease_id, origin_region, expiry, and a nonce to avoid replay.

kate: metrics wishlist: residency.handshake.latency_ms, residency.handshake.fail_rate, residency.forwarded_writes.total, residency.duplicate_writes.detected. also a per-tenant last_successful_lease timestamp for Console.

sre-bot: notice: observed handshake.failure spike during eu-west canary 2026-03-18. incident link: https://incidents.internal/2026-03-18-eviction-warmup

olivia: rollout plan: 1) RFC + unit tests, 2) feature-flagged canary for a few opt-in tenants, 3) proxy canary in single region, 4) chaos test (drop control plane messages), 5) expand. deny list tenants with strict legal residency until they opt-in.

dennis: testing matrix: token gen/verify unit tests, integration test for two-region concurrent-claim with injected clock skew, and e2e asserting idempotent final state across failure scenarios.

miguel: compatibility note: some older clients don't send X-Intent. proxy should detect write intent from HTTP semantics for known endpoints (POST /v1/streams/*) and treat conservatively. add changelog entry.

amanda: open question list: 1) Should proxies fully verify escrow signature or trust control plane-attached header? 2) Allow append-only partial-writes during swap window or require strict linearizability?

raj: my vote: proxies should verify. gives stronger audit trail and avoids a per-hop trusted intermediary. on 2) be conservative: require linearizable semantics now; append-only is a bigger contract change.

kate: Console needs events for per-tenant last-fallback, forwarded_writes stream with HTTP codes, and graphs for handshake latencies with percentile breakdowns. We'll add an operator-focused dashboard tile.

sre-bot: runbook update suggested: when residency.handshake.fail_rate > 0.5% over 10m alert and run cross-region-verify checklist.

amanda: I'll write a concise RFC with API samples, token format, key rotation, metrics, and rollout steps. will include a go snippet for token verification and a small proxy shim. owner mapping: amanda (control plane token), dennis (proxy changes), olivia (product gating), kate (metrics), miguel (compat).

miguel: can we include a tiny compatibility shim to map legacy headers to X-Intent? saves follow-ups.

amanda: good call. i'll add that to the proxy PR. timeline: RFC + tests by next Tue (1719999000), canary week after, GA after successful canary + chaos.

kate: :thumbsup: will add dashboard cards to the staging Console.

amanda: thanks all 1: will post RFC draft in #architecture/rfcs in a few hours. please review. :eyes:
